//: This is a Python project with exactly one authored JS/TS file:
to give typescript-language-server a *project boundary*, not to build
anything — `noEmit` is set and nothing ever runs `tsc`.
Without it tsserver has no tsconfig to anchor to, so it opens an
`inferred project` rooted at the repo and walks the whole tree. On a
working checkout that tree is not the 40 MB of tracked source: it is
4.2 GB, because vendor/ (2.5 GB), benchmarks/, docs/ and graphify-out/
accumulate untracked output. tsserver never finished the scan and never
published a diagnostic — 120 s of silence, which the engine reports the
same way it reports a clean file. Nothing errored; TypeScript support
was simply, quietly absent, and only on the host with the big tree.
`exclude` is therefore the load-bearing half of this file. `include`
keeps root-level scratch files (probes, one-off scripts) inside a
bounded project instead of spawning a fresh inferred one each time.
